# RealityCheck

RealityCheck is a local-first HTML note checker plus an evidence-first Web quality audit skill and CLI. The zero-install note checker reads selected HTML files only inside the user's browser and checks encoding, document structure, broken attachments, internal navigation, machine-specific paths, remote dependencies, executable scripts, mobile readability, accessibility, and unfinished AI placeholders. It can download JSON evidence, copy bilingual repair tasks, and generate a new conservatively repaired copy without overwriting the source. In an authorized Codex Skill task, `--prepare-repair` creates a bounded working copy with local assets so Codex can repair it directly, rerun the same check, and return before/after reports without asking the user to paste a report prompt back into Codex.

For professional Web QA, RealityCheck can preview a bilingual audit plan before browser access. It then uses a real installed Chrome, Edge, or Chromium browser to stress responsive layouts, user journeys, API and network recovery, links, publishing metadata, visual baselines, performance, accessibility, security policy, and aggregate Cookie/Web Storage privacy budgets. It writes bilingual human reports plus machine-readable JSON, SARIF, JUnit, repair plans, policy reviews, issue drafts, manifests, verification evidence, and freshness-aware GO/REVIEW/NO-GO release decisions.

RealityCheck never treats an unsupported check as passed. Audit mode is read-only, remote targets require explicit authorization, and generated GitHub issue drafts are local files that are never submitted automatically.

## Quick start

Open the zero-install checker and choose the original HTML export ZIP, one HTML file, or a note folder. One bounded ZIP32 STORE/DEFLATE archive is verified and extracted locally without execution or upload; unsafe, sensitive, encrypted, ZIP64, conflicting, damaged, special-file, hidden-record, or oversized input fails closed as a whole. Evidence keeps the exact source archive SHA-256, stable imported-content ID, HTML/CSS candidate ID, and final output manifest separate. Import a prior browser JSON to see new/resolved/worsened/persistent/unverified changes and download bilingual comparison evidence. A per-file repair still downloads one HTML only and labels folder assets unverified; a complete folder/ZIP can instead apply the three metadata fixes to every eligible HTML, run one cumulative package recheck, preserve the original root inside a new wrapper, and download only after a STORE ZIP read-back matches path/size/CRC32/SHA-256 proof. This online output is a working copy, not a publish verdict. For a no-clone local check, run `npx --yes --package="github:KevinwithPanda/RealityHTMLCheck#v0.11.0" realityhtmlcheck note ./my-notes`. For a verified passive-static host handoff, run the same package with `realityhtmlcheck publish ./my-notes`; only completed exact-final-ZIP Chromium gates receive the publish filename, while blocked or incomplete results remain explicit working copies. For recurring exports, use the Composite Action with `kind: publish`; it uploads only the parser-validated exact run, never deploys, and must disclose that an enabled GitHub Artifact contains the complete site bytes. RealityCheck never uploads from the local checker/CLI or deploys from any mode. Add `--fix-safe` for only the three conservative metadata repairs. Repeat `--exclude-html "archive/**"` only for reviewed archive/draft scope. Add `--baseline <prior-report.json>` for regression-only comparison, use the composite Action with `kind: note` for browser-free CI, or let the `$realitycheck` Skill use `--prepare-repair` for a complete agentic working copy without modifying the originals. To preview an existing Web project policy without browser access, run `npm run realitycheck -- plan --config realitycheck.config.json`. To audit an authorized local app, run `npm run audit -- http://localhost:3000`.
